text:
zoe: Heads-up: int4 canary (ceres-int4-stream) showing a small but actionable class of failures where the model emits \"action\" label tokens split across streaming chunks, resulting in either \"acti\" or \"on\" appearing as separate tokens and our parser not recognizing the field. Seen ~1.7% in the current canary.

marco: Any sample?

zoe: Example (raw captured output tokens flattened):
```
... , "tool_calls" : [ { "name": "search_db", "args": { "q": "foo" } } ], "ac t
ion" : "invoke_tool" ...
```
Note the space/newline in the middle of the label due to streaming chunk boundary. Parser expects exact key \"action\" so it fails.

chris: Is this purely streaming framing or something with int4 tokenization? Do we see it in non-streaming mirrors?

zoe: Mostly streaming. Non-streaming int4 mirrors show 0.05% (noise), but streaming int4 ~1.7%. fp16 streaming shows 0.12%. Correlates also with prompts that end with fenced code blocks or trailing JSON examples.

devops-bot: Canary summary: ceres-int4-stream (region-eu) 12/700 problematic = 1.71%. Baseline fp16-stream: 0.12%. Mirror logs: https://redwood.internal/canary/1799999000

arun: Two approaches: short-term parser hardening (normalize keys by stripping whitespace/newline inside tokens and casefold) + longer-term runtime fix (ensure streaming chunker doesn't split identifier tokens or adjust tokenization merging heuristics for int4 kernels).

marco: For parser hardening, we should be careful about false positives. If we coalesce broken keys, we might accidentally merge narrative fragments into keys. Proposal: only coalesce if the resulting key matches expected enum set (action, tool_calls, result) and if neighbor token context indicates JSON structure. Log an event when coalesce occurs.

chris: Agreed. Also add a verified-sample log that stores both raw tokens and reassembled JSON, plus a checksum of the original response, so we can reproduce exact failure later.

zoe: I'll push a reviver patch that: 1) trims inter-token whitespace/newline inside bareword keys when parsing streaming chunks, 2) casefolds keys, and 3) emits metric tag reviver=stream-coalesce-v1. Rolling to 3% of canary traffic.

devops-bot: Deploy started: reviver-stream-coalesce-v1 -> 2 nodes. Canary id c-ceres-r1.

marco: For the runtime side, I'll run an int4 kernel token-boundary test comparing q4_0 vs q4_1 kernels and streaming framing sizes (chunk=32/64/128 tokens) against /datasets/stream-edgecases. Will bench EOD.

arun: Also filed INF-8602 to extend raw-token retention for streaming parse errors to 72h.

zoe: Thanks. I'll post first 24h metrics here. If the reviver increases false positives we will throttle immediately. :thumbsup:
